question: A policy team keeps a handbook in a Drive folder that changes weekly, and also has one annual report that never changes. Which two set-ups fit best? Select two.
options: A) Connect the annual report and delete it from Drive, so that only one copy ever exists.
B) Upload the fixed annual report into Project knowledge, since its content will not change.
C) Paste the whole handbook into every new chat, so the newest version is always present.
D) Connect the Drive folder, so the weekly handbook changes are picked up from the source.
E) Upload a copy of the handbook just once and then rely on that copy for the rest of this year.
correct_answers: B) Upload the fixed annual report into Project knowledge, since its content will not change.
D) Connect the Drive folder, so the weekly handbook changes are picked up from the source.
explanations: Incorrect. Deleting the original to leave a single copy destroys the source of truth for no benefit.
Correct. A stable document is well suited to a one-time upload into Project knowledge, where it stays available to every chat.
Incorrect. Re-pasting a whole handbook per chat is the manual work Project knowledge and connectors exist to remove.
Correct. A connector reaches the live source, which is what a document that changes every week needs.
Incorrect. A one-time copy of a weekly-changing handbook goes stale fast and produces confidently outdated answers.
